rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lowered their heads in shame after Abraham had confuted them.
rows.anchor: خزيا قد حجهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says the people suffered a shameful disgrace.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: أصاب القوم خزية سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The powerless things worshipped besides God are their idols.
rows.anchor: يعني أصنامهم

words: أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproach was the device by which Abraham outwitted them.
rows.anchor: وهي التي كادهم بها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan recounts that people gathered firewood for a long time, even an elderly man who had rarely left home, as devotion to their idols.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: فجمعوا الحطب زمانا، حتى إن الشيخ الكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya had heard that Abraham was hurled into the fire by a catapult, the first use of one.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: بلغني أنهم رموا به في المنجنيق، فكان ذلك أول ما صنع المنجنيق

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali says the cold almost killed Abraham, so God added peace so it would not harm him.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال: قال الله: {يا نار كوني بردا} [الأنبياء: 69] فكادت تقتله من البرد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the blessing as safety from both the fire's heat and its cold.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {وسلاما} [الأنبياء: 69] يعني: وسلامة من حر النار ومن بردها

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says the fire harmed no one that day and burned nothing of Abraham except his bonds.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أن كعبا قال: ما انتفع بها يومئذ أحد من الناس، وما أحرقت منه يومئذ إلى وثاقه

rows.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
rows.claim: Bakr reports that creation and the rain angel asked permission to extinguish the fire; God said to help only if Abraham asked, then made the fire cool across east and west.
rows.anchor: عن بكر بن عبد الله المزني قال: إن إبراهيم لما أرادوا أن يلقوه في النار جاءت عامة الخليقة إلى ربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being admitted to God's mercy means being admitted to Paradise.
rows.anchor: يعني الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous here are the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: والصالحون هم أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man called Dhun-Nun is Jonah.
rows.anchor: يعني يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also calls Jonah the companion of the fish; nun means fish.
rows.anchor: وقال في آية أخرى: {كصاحب الحوت} [القلم: 48] والحوت، النون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan glosses his departure as enduring hardship for his Lord's religion.
rows.anchor: يعني مكابدا لدين ربه في تفسير الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says Jonah thought God would not punish him for what he had done.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: فظن أن لن نعاقبه بما صنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya recounts that Jonah warned his people of a fixed coming punishment; they repented in humility, and God turned it away, but Jonah returned to find the city unchanged and left in distress.
rows.anchor: وبلغنا أن يونس دعا قومه زمانا إلى الله عز وجل، فلما طال ذلك وأبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Jonah's prayer, God answered and rescued him by ordering the fish to cast him onto land.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى الحوت أن يلقيه إلى البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya says Jonah was weak on the bare shore, like a nursing infant.
rows.anchor: وهو ضعيف مثل الصبي الرضيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's heat afflicted Jonah, so God shaded him with a gourd; when it withered he grieved, and God admonished him for grieving over a plant while wishing to destroy a hundred thousand or more people.
rows.anchor: فأصابته حرارة الشمس، فأنبت الله عليه تبارك وتعالى {شجرة من يقطين} [الصافات: 146] وهي القرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah found a flock, miraculously milked a sheep said to have no milk, and identified himself to its shepherd; the sheep and a tree later testified to his presence when the people feared breaking their oath not to lie.
rows.anchor: فأخذ شاة منها فمسح بيده على ظهرها، فدرت فشرب من لبنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nineveh, Jonah's city, is in the land of Mosul on the Tigris.
rows.anchor: وهي مدينة يقال لها: نينوى من أرض الموصل، وهي على دجلة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jonah boarded a boat on the Tigris, was swallowed, reached the sea, then returned by the Tigris and was cast onto its shore.
rows.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عباس قال: في دجلة ركب السفينة، وفيها التقمه الحوت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the darknesses as the sea, the night, and the fish's belly.
rows.anchor: وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Jonah meant that he had sinned.
rows.anchor: يعني بخطيئته. تفسير السدي

words: لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says this was the prayer of Dhun-Nun inside the fish, and that no Muslim uses it to supplicate God for anything without receiving an answer.
rows.anchor: عن جده سعد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " دعوة ذي النون إذ دعا وهو في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Zechariah's prayer by giving him John and restoring his wife.
rows.anchor: قوله: {وزكريا إذ نادى ربه رب لا تذرني فردا وأنت خير الوارثين} [الأنبياء: 89] فاستجاب الله له

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says Zechariah's wife was barren and God made her fertile.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت عاقرا فجعلها الله ولودا

rows.speaker: بعض التابعين
rows.claim: A Successor says Zechariah's wife had a long tongue.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان عن بعض التابعين قال: كان في لسانها طول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hastening in good things means doing righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: يعني الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is that resurrection will certainly occur.
rows.anchor: يعني: كائنا، البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God is the one who will do it.
rows.anchor: أي نحن فاعلون

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses al-Zabur as the books, including Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an, and al-dhikr as the heavenly register, the Mother of the Book.
rows.anchor: تفسير مجاهد: يعني بالزبور الكتب، التوراة، والإنجيل، والقرآن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's interpretation identifies the earth promised to the righteous as Paradise.
rows.anchor: {أن الأرض} [الأنبياء: 105] يعني أرض الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Zabur as David's Psalms, the Reminder as the Torah, and the inheriting righteous servants as Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير ابن عباس: {ولقد كتبنا في الزبور} [الأنبياء: 105] يعني زبور داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is meant by this is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قوله: {إن في هذا} [الأنبياء: 106] القرآن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid includes Mecca, pilgrimage, lesser pilgrimage, and all sins God has forbidden among His sacred limits.
rows.anchor: تفسير مجاهد الحرمات: مكة، والحج، والعمرة، وما نهى الله عنه من معاصيه كلها

words: وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusions recited in this verse are the forbidden foods listed in the Qur'an's dietary passage.
rows.anchor: في سورة المائدة من: {الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به

words: وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also links the rule to the prohibition on hunting while in ihram.
rows.anchor: قال: {غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم} [المائدة: 1] وقد فسرت ذلك في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoid idols because they are impure.
rows.anchor: اجتنبوا الأوثان فإنها رجس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: False speech means lying about God, that is, associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: وقول الزور: الكذب على الله يعني الشرك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives the broader gloss that false speech means lying.
rows.anchor: أن مجاهدا قال: الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers have prospered by becoming happy; the happy ones are the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: قد سعد المؤمنون، والسعداء أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says God made only Adam, the Torah, and Paradise with His hand; He told Paradise to speak, and it spoke this verse.
rows.anchor: أن كعبا قال: لم يخلق الله بيده إلا ثلاثة، خلق آدم بيده، وكتب التوراة بيده

rows.speaker: المعلى بن هلال
rows.claim: Al-Mu'alla reports that God built Paradise with gold and silver bricks and musk mortar, filled it, spoke this verse, then closed it so no angel or prophet knows what is inside; the dawn's coolness and scent escape through its door.
rows.anchor: المعلى بن هلال ذكره بإسناد قال: إن الله خلق الجنة بيده، فجعل لبنة ذهب، ولبنة فضة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains humility in prayer as fear firmly settled in the heart.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال: الخشوع: الخوف الثابت في القلب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains humility as lowering the gaze and being gentle and subdued.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الخشوع: غض البصر وخفض الجناح

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says scholars disliked fidgeting with the hands, looking around, or occupying the mind with worldly matters during prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان أهل العلم يكرهون إذا قام الرجل في صلاته أن يعبث بشيء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud prayed with lowered gaze, hands, and voice.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة أن عبد الله بن مسعود كان إذا قام في الصلاة خفض فيها بصره

rows.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says people used to look around in prayer until this verse came down, after which they lowered their eyes and seemed to look at the place of prostration.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال: كانوا يلتفتون في صلاتهم حتى نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan also glosses the humble as fearful.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] أي خائفون

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says laghw means falsehood.
rows.anchor: وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses equate laghw with lies and ultimately with associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: ويقال: الكذب. وهو واحد، وهو الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They perform the obligatory alms payment.
rows.anchor: يؤدون الزكاة المفروضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guarding their private parts means avoiding adultery.
rows.anchor: من الزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man may marry one, two, three, or four wives, but more than four are not lawful.
rows.anchor: إن شاء تزوج واحدة، وإن شاء تزوج اثنتين، وإن شاء ثلاثا، وإن شاء أربعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man may have intercourse with as many enslaved women as he owns.
rows.anchor: يطأ بملك يمينه كم شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no blame or sin in intercourse with wives or enslaved women.
rows.anchor: لا لوم عليهم في ذلك، أي لا إثم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking beyond one's wives or enslaved women is transgression; the transgressors are adulterers who cross from lawful to forbidden.
rows.anchor: {فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك} [المؤمنون: 7] وراء أزواجه أو ما ملكت يمينه. {فأولئك هم العادون} [المؤمنون: 7] الزناة تعدوا الحلال إلى الحرام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says whoever goes beyond what is lawful falls into what is forbidden.
rows.anchor: وكان قتادة يقول: من تعدى الحلال أصاب الحرام

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the transgressors as people who wrong themselves by committing sin.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {فأولئك هم العادون} [المؤمنون: 7] أي: فأولئك هم المعتدون، أي: الظالمون أنفسهم بركوب المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They discharge trusts and fulfill covenants.
rows.anchor: يؤدون الأمانة ويوفون بالعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They guard the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: يحافظون على الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says prayer observance includes its ablution, appointed times, bowing, and prostration.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: على وضوئها، ومواقيتها، وركوعها، وسجودها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever maintains the five prayers with their ablution, times, bowing, and prostration, recognizing God's claim upon him, enters Paradise or has Paradise guaranteed.
rows.anchor: عن حنظلة الكاتب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من حافظ على الصلوات الخمس، على وضوئهن ومواقيتهن

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa'id adds that such a person is barred from the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد: حرم على النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone has a home and family prepared in Paradise; if someone disobeys, that home is transferred to a believer, who thereby inherits the homes and spouses prepared for believers.
rows.anchor: ليس من واحد إلا قد أعد الله له منزلا وأهلا في الجنة، فإن أطاع الله صار إلى ما أعد له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says al-Firdaws is one of Paradise's names.
rows.anchor: والفردوس اسم من أسماء الجنة في تفسير الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya had heard that the word al-Firdaws is Roman.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: وبلغني أنها بالرومية

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that al-Firdaws is a hill of Paradise, its center and finest part.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: هي ربوة الجنة، وأوسطها، وأفضلها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says al-Firdaws is a mountain in Paradise from which its rivers flow.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: الفردوس: جبل في الجنة تفجر منه أنهار الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Noah's people and their drowning contains signs for those who came after them.
rows.anchor: {إن في ذلك لآيات} [المؤمنون: 30] من أمر قوم نوح وغرقهم {لآيات} [المؤمنون: 30] لمن بعدهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets the testing as the religion brought by the messengers: worship of God.
rows.anchor: وهو تفسير الحسن

words: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later people created after Noah were the people of 'Ad.
rows.anchor: {ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم} [المؤمنون: 31] من بعد نوح. {قرنا آخرين} [المؤمنون: 31] يعني عادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger sent to 'Ad was Hud.
rows.anchor: يعني هودا

words: أن اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud called them to worship God alone and asked whether they would not be wary.
rows.anchor: أن اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's granting them ease in worldly life means that He expanded their provision.
rows.anchor: وسعنا الدنيا عليهم، أي في الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs argued that Hud was a human like them who ate and drank as they did, and that obeying him in his call would make them losers.
rows.anchor: ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs call the believers losers by calling them weak and incapable.
rows.anchor: يعني لعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is spoken by some chiefs to one another.
rows.anchor: يقوله بعضهم لبعض على الاستفهام

words: إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mock the promise that people will be brought out after death and decay, denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: مبعوثون. أي قد وعدكم ذلك، تكذبون بالبعث

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says resurrection seemed remote to them, so they said it would not happen.
rows.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة قال: تباعد البعث في أنفس القوم، أي لا يبعثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that they die and live means that they die and are born.
rows.anchor: أي نموت ونولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man they accuse of inventing a lie about God is Hud.
rows.anchor: يعنون هودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs say Hud falsely claims that God sent him.
rows.anchor: يزعم أن الله أرسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean that they do not believe him.
rows.anchor: أي: بمصدقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud asks his Lord for help because his people denied him, and God answers.
rows.anchor: {قال رب انصرني بما كذبون {39} قال} [المؤمنون: 39-40] الله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the phrase means after a short time.
rows.anchor: أي: عن قليل. والميم والألف صلة في الكلام. وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says they will soon regret their rejection, then seizes them with the blast.
rows.anchor: قال الله: {فأخذتهم الصيحة بالحق} [المؤمنون: 41] تفسير الحسن: الصيحة: العذاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains the blast as punishment.
rows.anchor: تفسير الحسن: الصيحة: العذاب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, through al-Mu'alla and Abu Yahya, compares the people made into debris to something decayed.
rows.anchor: في تفسير المعلى عن أبي يحيى عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some compare them to vegetation that is crushed after it was green.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: مثل النبات إذا صار غثاء، فتهشم بعد إذ كان أخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers driven away are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: المشركين

words: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرونا آخرين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created other generations after the earlier peoples had perished.
rows.anchor: من بعد الهالكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation has a fixed time of destruction; none can delay it or advance it by even an hour.
rows.anchor: يعني الوقت الذي يهلكها فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word they should reflect on is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن

words: أم جاءهم ما لم يأت آباءهم الأولين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya reads the question as saying that the message came to them just as it had come to their forefathers.
rows.anchor: أي: لم يأتهم إلا ما أتى آباءهم الأولين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi instead says the Qur'an is something that had not come to their forefathers.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {أم جاءهم ما لم يأت} [المؤمنون: 68] يعني الذي لم يأت آباءهم الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger they know is Muhammad, sent to them.
rows.anchor: أي: الذي أرسلهم إليهم، يعني محمدا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says they knew Muhammad's face and lineage.
rows.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة قال: بل يعرفون وجهه ونسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did accuse Muhammad of madness.
rows.anchor: أي بمحمد جنون. أي قد قالوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth Muhammad brought is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: {بل جاءهم بالحق} [المؤمنون: 70] القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who hate the truth are the group among them who did not believe.
rows.anchor: يعني جماعة من لم يؤمن منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The desires in question are those of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: أهواء المشركين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says that if truth followed their desires, those desires would bring ruin on the heavens, earth, and everyone in them.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الحسن: لو كان الحق في أهوائهم، لوقعت أهواؤهم على هلاك السموات والأرض ومن فيهن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret al-haqq here as God, citing the command to counsel one another with truth as meaning God and with patience as steadfastness in His duties.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الحق هاهنا: الله، كقوله: {وتواصوا بالحق} [العصر: 3] يعني بالحق: الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is their honor, which whoever believes in the Qur'an receives.
rows.anchor: بشرفهم، شرف لمن آمن به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatadah say the reminder is the Qur'an, which teaches what people should do and avoid, and what is forbidden and permitted.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: يعني القرآن، أنزلنا عليهم فيه ما يأتون، وما يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn away from what God has explained to them.
rows.anchor: عما بينا لهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah identifies the reminder they reject as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: معرضون عن القرآن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reads both references to the reminder as their honor: they turn away from their own honor.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {بل أتيناهم بذكرهم} [المؤمنون: 71] : بشرفهم {فهم عن ذكرهم} [المؤمنون: 71] يعني عن شرفهم

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri cites 21:10, where the Book is described as containing their mention, and takes mention to mean honor.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: سمعت سفيان الثوري يذكر في هذه الآية: {لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم} [الأنبياء: 10] : فيه شرفكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says the question means: do you ask them a payment for what you brought? The implied answer is no.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: أم تسألهم على ما أتيتهم به جعلا، أي إنك لا تسألهم عليه أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward from God in the Hereafter is better than any worldly wage they might pay.
rows.anchor: أجر ربك أي ثوابه في الآخرة خير من أجرهم لو أعطوك في الدنيا أجرا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: God is the best provider: He may provide people through one another, allotting one person's provision through another's hands.
rows.anchor: وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: أم الدرداء
rows.claim: Umm al-Darda says God does not send coins from heaven but provides through people; accept provision that comes, use it if needed, otherwise pass it to needy brethren, and do not reject God's provision.
rows.anchor: عن أم الدرداء قالت: ما بال أحدكم يقول: اللهم ارزقني، وقد علم أن الله لا يمطر عليه من السماء دنانير ولا دراهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Umar to accept a gift he had neither sought nor pursued, then spend it if needed or give it to those in need.
rows.anchor: عن عمران القصير قال: لقيت مكحولا بمكة، فأعطاني شيئا فانقبضت عنه فقال: خذه

rows.speaker: قبيصة بن ذؤيب
rows.claim: Qubaysa reports that Umar gave Qurayshi Abdullah ibn Sa'd a thousand dinars and urged him to accept an unsolicited gift, as the Prophet had instructed Umar.
rows.anchor: عن قبيصة بن ذؤيب أن عمر بن الخطاب دفع إلى عبد الله بن سعد، رجل من قريش، ألف دينار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path Muhammad calls them to is the sound religion and the road to Paradise.
rows.anchor: إلى دين مستقيم، وهو الطريق إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Belief in the Hereafter here means belief in resurrection on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: يعني بالبعث يوم القيامة. وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah glosses turning away from the path as deviating from it.
rows.anchor: لجائرون في تفسير قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says they have left the path.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: تاركون له

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says they turn away from the path; Yahya says these glosses amount to the same thing.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: معرضون عنه. قال يحيى: وهو واحد

words: ولو رحمناهم وكشفنا ما بهم من ضر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are Meccans afflicted by seven years of hunger so severe they ate carrion and bones and imagined smoke between themselves and the sky; the smoke verse preceded the famine, and Yahya says they would persist in error even if relieved.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل مكة، وذلك حيث أخذوا بالجوع سبع سنين حتى أكلوا الميتة والعظام

words: ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This question is put to the people while they are in Hell.
rows.anchor: يقول لهم ذلك في النار

rows.speaker: ابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Mujahid, quoting his father, says their misery was what had been written for them.
rows.anchor: تفسير ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: التي كتبت علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit that they were a people gone astray.
rows.anchor: وكنا قوما ضالين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says a wretched person is wretched in the womb, while a happy person learns from another's fate.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل قال: سمعت عبد الله بن مسعود يقول: الشقي من شقي في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya notes that the Prophet's report that a person's wretchedness or happiness is written in the womb was discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا الحديث عن النبي عليه السلام أنه يكتب في بطن أمه شقيا أو سعيدا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Amr reports that Hell's inhabitants call Malik for forty years without reply, hear that they will remain, then call God and wait twice the world's lifespan before being told to be cast away and stop speaking; afterward they only groan and gasp like donkeys.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن أهل جهنم يدعون مالكا فلا يجيبهم أربعين عاما

rows.speaker: سليمان التيمي
rows.claim: Al-Taymi reports that Hell's inhabitants call the keepers for forty years, Malik for eighty years, then God for twice the world's lifespan; they receive the replies in 40:50, 43:77, and 23:108 and thereafter only groan and gasp.
rows.anchor: عن سليمان التيمي أن أهل النار يدعون خزنة أهل النار أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wise means wise in His command.
rows.anchor: {حكيم} [النور: 18] في أمره

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says the shameful deed people want spread is adultery becoming public.
rows.anchor: في تفسير قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses spreading the shameful deed as its becoming widespread, close to Qatadah's explanation that it appears publicly.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {أن تشيع الفاحشة} [النور: 19] يعني تفشو

words: في الذين آمنوا لهم عذاب أليم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who desire the scandal among believers are hypocrites seeking to disgrace and anger the Prophet.
rows.anchor: هم المنافقون. كانوا يحبون ذلك ليعيبوا به النبي ويغيظوه

words: لهم عذاب أليم في الدنيا والآخرة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly punishment is that they must pay alms and contribute to military campaigns unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وعذاب الدنيا للمنافقين أن تؤخذ منهم الزكاة كرها، وما ينفقون في الغزو كرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in the preceding verse, God's grace and mercy kept Him from destroying and wiping out the people who made these accusations.
rows.anchor: هي مثل الأولى، أي لأهلكهم فاستأصلهم. يعني الذين قالوا ما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya says the grace and mercy here do not refer to Abdullah ibn Ubayy, whom the following passage places in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وليس يعني بالفضل والرحمة عبد الله بن أبي ابن سلول فيهم. وقد ذكره بعد هذه الآية أنه في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is compassionate and merciful toward the believers.
rows.anchor: بالمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The steps of Satan mean sins.
rows.anchor: قوله: {يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات} [النور: 21] خطايا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the steps are Satan's commands.
rows.anchor: {الشيطان} [النور: 21] وبعضهم يقول: أمر الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in this clause refers to Satan.
rows.anchor: فإن الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan commands people to sin and to commit shameful and wrongful deeds.
rows.anchor: بالخطيئة ويأمر

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abu Majliz says the steps of Satan include vows to commit sins.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: {لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان} [النور: 21] قال: النذور في المعاصي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says there is no valid vow made in anger and its expiation is the expiation for an oath.
rows.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا نذر في غضب وكفارته كفارة اليمين»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about God's grace and mercy repeats the explanation just given for the earlier occurrence.
rows.anchor: هي مثل الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that none of you would have become righteous.
rows.anchor: ما صلح منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God purifies means that God makes people righteous.
rows.anchor: من أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي
